source.title: To Asymmetry and Beyond: Structured Pruning of Sequence to Sequence Models for Improved Inference Efficiency

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream summarization performance across model sizes in a new setting, using ROUGE rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-set ROUGE-2 for unpruned FLAN-T5 models at three sizes on three summarization datasets; these results bear on V6. The pruning and inference-efficiency results do not measure the loss laws, compute-optimal allocation, or other named versions.
record.test_reason: Section 3.2 fine-tunes FLAN-T5 small, base and large on three summarization datasets and reports test ROUGE as a function of model size. This is a weak downstream-scaling result bearing on V6. It has only three sizes, one run each, no fitted relation and no loss measurement. The pruning and latency results do not measure any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors' main conclusion is that asymmetric pruning, mainly pruning the decoder, gives about 3x inference speedup for about 1 ROUGE-2 point loss. They add that larger models lose less accuracy when pruned, and that summarization quality rises with scale with substantial variation across datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates fine-tuned FLAN-T5 summarization models using ROUGE, rather than measuring held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fitting parameter, token, and compute scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scale-related ROUGE gains vary by dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger FLAN-T5 models lose less ROUGE-2 under the same layer pruning. Example: QIWS 1/6 encoder+decoder keeps 21% of ROUGE-2 for small vs 61% for large (Tables 5-7, 19-24).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness of fine-tuned models to structured pruning increases with model scale.

record.problems: The study trains each model once and does not optimize parameters for each model. It reports no uncertainty for the ROUGE results and tests only three model sizes and three summarization datasets; it does not report loss-law fits or predictive validation.
record.rows_left_out: Pruning and inference-efficiency results in Tables 5-10 and 16-33 are not extracted: they concern compression and latency rather than the tested unpruned performance-versus-scale trend. Other summarization metrics are omitted because ROUGE-2 is the main scale-comparison metric used in the cited tables.

untested.parts: Any fitted or predictive relation (power law, or prediction from pretraining loss); sizes beyond 750M; multiple seeds; tasks other than summarization.
Not tested: no pretraining loss reported.
Not tested: no extrapolation from fits.
Not tested: layer pruning changes parameter count, so shape is not held at fixed size.
Not tested: fine-tuning results are not fitted to any power-law form.
Not tested: no fitting choices are examined.

record.verdict_notes: Paper calls this a study of 'scaling laws' but fits no law. Rows rely on appendix Tables 13-15. Main-text Tables 2 and 4 have swapped dataset captions. Each model was trained once with shared hyperparameters, so the base-to-large XSUM flattening may reflect training noise. Other ROUGE metrics show the same trend and are declared left out.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from fits to small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as compute changes.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count and their effect on loss.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study measures summarization ROUGE-2 at three model sizes, but does not fit a predictive relation, test pretraining-loss-to-task-performance prediction, or assess other downstream tasks.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices and setup.

relationships.condition: Unpruned fine-tuned FLAN-T5 on QIWS, CNNDM and XSUM
relationships.reason: ROUGE-2 increases monotonically small to base to large on all three datasets: QIWS 29.03/34.19/37.37, CNNDM 17.55/19.77/21.15, XSUM 11.09/15.69/16.34 (r2, r3, r5, r6, r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: ROUGE-2 increased from small to base to large on QIWS (29.03/34.19/37.37), CNNDM (17.55/19.77/21.15), and XSUM (11.09/15.69/16.34).

relationships.reason: Gain nearly stalls on XSUM (+0.65 ROUGE-2 for 3.4x parameters vs +4.6 for small to base), and size of gain varies strongly by dataset (r8, r9). Single runs with no tuned hyperparameters.
relationships.display_finding: A 3.4-fold parameter increase added only 0.65 ROUGE-2, versus 4.6 from small to base, in single runs without hyperparameter tuning.
